100.key_question: Is the unit-1 gradient conflict a stable property of the task (unit 1 needs a different conversion) or transient noise of early training?

200.key_question: When the block becomes causal (IIA >= 0.5), does it keep this equivalence-preserving geometry (shared code across units) or does it split into unit routes as in the seed-700 network?

300.key_question: Where is equivalence computed during the plateau, if not causally in the block?

400.key_question: Is the rising interaction an early unit-specific rotation that will become the formation-time route split, or noise in a block that still carries little mass variance?

500.key_question: How much of the lineage-event stream is matching ambiguity rather than real change, and how should it be reported?

600.key_question: Will the circle form before causal use again (a reproducible ordering across seeds), and will the route split accompany it?

700.key_question: Is the reorganisation leading toward formation (a causal mass code) or is the plateau extending?

800.key_question: What is the network learning during the plateau, if not mass? Candidate: the answer distribution conditioned on zero-status and the output unit.

900.key_question: Will the network escape the zero-plus-constant plateau on its own (as other mass_only seeds did), and does escape happen through the mass block or elsewhere?

1000.key_question: Which candidate function will rise above baseline first, and does the shared block geometry need to dissolve before the causal mass code can form?

1100.key_question: Which head will become the dominant mass writer, and will it inherit the unit-1 split from the value token?

1200.key_question: Does the editable code at formation survive consolidation, or does the interaction between mass and unit route grow and erase editability (the seed-700 trajectory)?

1300.key_question: Can the layer-1 binding be made compositional (value code rotated by unit scale) so held-out combinations form correct mass, without losing what the network already does?

1400.key_question: Is there any organisational defect worth repairing, or only the generalisation gap, which is upstream and outside the registered primitives' reach?

1500.key_question: What information does the residual interaction carry that helps held-out combinations, given that the held-out failure is mostly upstream (step 1,300)?

1600.key_question: Does the network return to the same organisation after the spike (attractor, as in doc 27), and does editability recover fully?

1700.key_question: Can held-out mass formation be improved without removing the unit-specific geometry that partly compensates?

1800.key_question: Is there any remaining organisational property worth improving whose improvement would not cost generalisation?

1900.key_question: How large is the natural checkpoint-to-checkpoint variance of OOD_DEV after convergence (needed to interpret any B-A difference at 6,000)?

2000.key_question: Is the erosion transient (OOD recovers, as accuracy did after the 1,600 spike) or a monotone trend to the end of training?
